Do you love gaming, social media and creator culture - and do you know how to make a global brand feel local?

We are looking for a Brand Engagement & Community Specialist for Denmark to join PlayStation Nordic as a fixed-term maternity cover from 1st January 2027 to 1st of February 2028.

This role sits in our Marketing team and is all about bringing PlayStation closer to players every day through social media, influencer collaborations, local content and community management.

This is a hands-on role. You will not just sit in meetings talking about campaigns. You will help make them happen.

You will work closely with our Leads across social media, PR, influencers, brand partnerships, sponsorships and campaigns - and you will be one of the people making sure PlayStation shows up in a way that feels relevant, local and real.

**What you'll be doing

**Social media, content and community

You will help run PlayStation’s Danish social channels day to day. That means planning, publishing, adapting content, engaging with the community and making sure our tone feels right for our Danish audience.

You will work with global assets, Danish ideas and real-time opportunities across channels like Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and other relevant platforms.

In practice, this means:

• Adapting global PlayStation content so it works in Danish language, tone and context

• Supporting the local social media calendar

• Publishing and scheduling content (in collaboration with student assistant)

• Managing community engagement and comments

• Spotting local trends and moments we can react to

• Supporting live coverage around events, campaigns and sponsorships

• Making sure our content feels like PlayStation, but also like it belongs locally

You will also collaborate with the Danish student assistant on relevant tasks such as translations, content adaptations and community work.

Influencers and creators

Creators are a big part of how we bring PlayStation to life in the Nordics. You will support our local influencer work, from finding the right profiles to briefing, seeding and following up on content.

You will work closely with our PR & Influencer Lead, but you will also be expected to take ownership of the day-to-day coordination in the Danish market.

This includes:

• Building and maintaining relationships with Danish creators and PlayStation Playmakers

• Supporting influencer briefings, seedings and content follow-up

• Coordinating products, merchandise and hardware where relevant

• Tracking creator content and helping report on performance

• Making sure creators are properly briefed and aligned with PlayStation guidelines

Campaign and partnership support

You will be involved in some of the biggest PlayStation moments of the year. That can be major game launches, hardware pushes, UEFA sponsorship activations, retail collaborations, influencer events or local content ideas.

You will help turn strategy into actual execution.

That means:

• Supporting priority campaigns in the Danish market

• Contributing with local ideas and cultural input

• Helping execute brand partnership and sponsorship activations

• Supporting events, press moments and consumer activations

• Working in Monday.com to keep tasks, owners and deadlines clear

• Making sure local execution is on time and on brief

What we are looking for

We are looking for someone who is structured, curious and genuinely interested in gaming, social media and online communities.

You do not need to know everything from day one. But you do need to be proactive, willing to learn and comfortable working in a team where many things move at the same time.

You probably bring:

• Danish at native level, especially written Danish

• Strong English skills

• Good understanding of social media and creator culture

• A strong feel for what works in Denmark

• Good writing skills and attention to tone of voice

• Confidence in coordinating tasks and keeping projects moving

• Good attention to detail

• Ability to work with several stakeholders at once

• Interest in gaming, entertainment and online communities

• Experience with social media, influencer work, content production, communications or marketing

• Familiarity with tools like Monday.com, Upfluence or Emplifi is a plus, but not a requirement

Most importantly, you are someone people enjoy working with. We need someone who can take responsibility, communicate clearly and help make the team better.

What can you expect?

You will join a team that cares deeply about PlayStation, but also about doing good work together.

We are a Nordic team working across multiple markets, cultures and disciplines. Some days are structured. Some days are messy. That is part of the job. But you will be close to great campaigns, major game launches, creators, communities and some of the biggest entertainment moments of the year.

You will get responsibility, trust and room to contribute.

Application task

Please apply by using the "Apply Now". We do not receive applications via. e-mail.

As part of your application, we would like you to include a short video of max. 1 minute.

In the video, please answer this question in Danish:

• Tell us about something you are proud of creating, improving or making happen.

This does not need to be professionally produced. We are not looking for editing skills or a polished influencer video. We are interested in how you think and how you communicate.

Our application system cannot receive video files, so please upload the video to YouTube, Vimeo or a similar platform and include the link in your application. An unlisted link is completely fine.

Application deadline is 22/10/2026.

About Nordisk Film

Nordisk Film was founded in 1906 in Valby, by entrepreneur Ole Olsen and is one of the world’s first film companies. They still have their headquarters in Valby, next to the world’s oldest film studio building and still own strong cultural values of passion and ambition.

In 1992, Nordisk Film became part of Egmont, a Nordic media group, and has within recent years seen high growth rates. In just over five years their revenues have increased with nearly 40%, and activities now span much wider than the film business that was the starting point. Today, Nordisk Film is among the leading entertainment companies in the Nordics involved in film and series production and distribution, cinemas, computer games, digital gifting and digital advertising.

For more than 20 years, and since the launch of Sony PlayStation, Nordisk Film Interactive has been the official distributor of the console and games in the Nordics and Baltics, and have made it one of Sony’s most successful markets.

jobs.occupation: Specialist/Consultant in Neurology looking for job opportunities in Denmark?
jobs.description:
Specialist/Consultant in Neurology looking for job opportunities in Denmark?

Newly Created Position at Mid- and West Zealand Hospital for an Emergency Neurology Profile in Partnership with Rigshospitalet, The University Hospital of Copenhagen.

We are expanding our team of specialists at Mid- and West Zealand Hospital, Denmark as we develop a new emergency neurology profile. You will have a direct professional influence on our future emergency services and become part of a new, close partnership with Rigshospitalet.

Why choose us?

• Help shape the emergency services of the future: You will play a central role in developing and launching our upcoming emergency neurology profile (without a thrombolysis service).

• New partnership with Rigshospitalet: The collaboration will open opportunities for professional exchange, knowledge sharing and research. For those interested, there will also be opportunities for attractive split appointments (e.g. one day per week at Rigshospitalet).

• New professional opportunities from 1 January 2027: As a result of the healthcare reform in Denmark, we will take over specialised rehabilitation from the municipalities, creating exciting opportunities for professional development.

• Scope for your subspecialty: Whether your interests lie in MS, movement disorders, headache, dementia, epilepsy or rehabilitation, we will adapt the framework to allow you to pursue your area of expertise.

• A strong research environment: We focus on patients with multimorbidity and have our own Professor of Neurology. Research is primarily focused on multiple sclerosis.

Your profile

You are a specialist/consultant in neurology, whether you are newly qualified and eager to develop your skills or an experienced colleague looking for a new professional setting.

We imagine that you:

• Are passionate about multidisciplinary collaboration and want to help shape the quality of the new emergency setup.

• Value a strong professional network across hospitals.

• Appreciate the opportunity to provide clinical guidance and supervision to our junior doctors.

• Are decisive, flexible and actively contribute to our positive working environment and pioneering spirit.

Your working day and responsibilities

Our department provides primary-level neurological services in the hospital at Slagelse (inpatient ward for phase II rehabilitation, primarily for apoplexy cases, as well as specialist clinics), and in the hospital of Naestved, where we run the Centre for Neurorehabilitation (CNN), which provides services at regional level.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Working in our outpatient department, specialist clinics or the interdisciplinary Memory Clinic, in collaboration with geriatricians, psychiatrists and neuropsychologists.

• Supervising junior doctors and participating in the multidisciplinary environment across our hospital sites.

• On-call duties: Our consultants currently cover the senior on-call function on site until 9.00 pm, followed by an on-call-from-home arrangement (there is junior on-call doctor is present on site around the clock).

About the department

Neurology is part of a combined department (Medicine 3 and Department of Physio- and Occupational Therapy) that works closely and efficiently alongside the Department of Geriatrics. We place a strong emphasis on professional dialogue and peer support within a group of doctors characterised by strong collegial relationships and a shared desire to develop the specialty.

Mid- and West Zealand Hospital is located around 60 min. by car from central Copenhagen.

Practical information and application

• The seven medical roles: Your application should address the seven medical competencies specifically, supported by the best possible documentation.

• Interests: If you have specific wishes regarding subspecialisation or are interested in a split appointment with Rigshospitalet, we would be pleased if you mention this in your application.

Relocation Assistance and Danish Language Tutoring

When you relocate to Denmark in connection with your employment, we offer free, professional assistance with relocation and settling in, either close to the hospital or anywhere on Zealand you might prefer. You will receive help with everything from finding accommodation to registration and arrangements for any accompanying family members.

An important part of working as a doctor in Denmark is communication between you and your patients and colleagues. For patient safety reasons, Region Zealand therefore requires our doctors to have a satisfactory level of Danish language proficiency. We therefore provide a language teacher for one-to-one tuition, enabling you to communicate with your patients as quickly as possible at a level where you can understand one another.

This means, that we expect you to be prepared to devote time to learning Danish, both spoken and written as part of your employment.

Find out more about what kind of assistance we offer, as well as watch interviews with other doctors that have relocated to Region Zealand at www.medicaljobsdenmark.com.

Would you like to know more?

You are very welcome to contact Chief Physician Benedikte Wanscher on mobile +45 93 57 62 51 or by email at bewa@regionsjaelland.dk for an informal and confidential conversation about the position.

Please upload your application and CV as soon as possible. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.

Ansættelsesområde

Region Sjælland og Region Hovedstaden bliver den 1. januar 2027 til Region Østdanmark som følge af sundhedsreformen. Dit ansættelsesområde vil være Region Østdanmark med alle tilhørende organisatoriske enheder.

Læs mere om betydningen af ansættelsesområdet på Region Østdanmarks hjemmeside.

Startløn for overenskomstansatte

Regionen er forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startlønnen for stillingen. Du får oplyst grundløn, centralt fastsatte tillæg og pension i den relevante overenskomst. Udover startlønnen, kan lønnen indeholde eventuelt forhandlede tillæg afhængigt af stillingen, dine erfaringer og kvalifikationer.

Se startlønnen på regionens hjemmeside

Om Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital arbejder vi hver dag for at fremme det sunde liv ved at forebygge og behandle i en sammenhængende sundhedsindsats. Som hospital forener vi psykiatri og somatik. Vores mål er, at patienter og borgere oplever gode og trygge forløb af høj kvalitet.

Som medarbejder bliver du en del af et nytænkende, fagligt og organisatorisk robust hospital, hvor vi gør en forskel for de mennesker, der har brug for os. Læring og udvikling er en del af hverdagen og sker i fagligt forpligtende fællesskaber. Også på tværs af afdelinger.

Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital dækker et opland på ca. 230.000 borgere. Vi har 766 sengepladser og er omkring 5.000 ansatte fordelt på 20 afdelinger, herunder 16 somatiske og psykiatriske specialer.

Vi tilbyder et solidt forskningsmiljø med 13 professorer og et stærkt fagligt uddannelsesmiljø, hvor vi hvert år byder cirka 2.700 studerende, elever og læger i videreuddannelsesforløb velkommen.

jobs.occupation: Associate Project Director, Global Regulatory Affairs & Patient Safety
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about translating strategic priorities into disciplined execution? Do you have extensive experience leading complex, cross-functional projects in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry? If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Associate Project Director, GRAPS.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking an experienced and highly structured Associate Project Director to join our GRAPS Enablement & Insights function within Global Regulatory Affairs & Patient Safety.

In this role, you will translate GRAPS priorities into integrated plans and disciplined execution across Global Regulatory Affairs, Global Patient Safety, and key enterprise functions. You will lead strategic and operational initiatives involving multiple functions, geographies, vendors, and systems, while establishing clear governance, decision pathways, performance reporting, and risk management.

This is an exciting opportunity to combine strategic perspective with hands-on project leadership in a global and highly regulated environment. You will work closely with the GRAPS Leadership Team, functional leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen quality, compliance, predictability, and organizational scalability.

You will join the GRAPS team (Global Regulatory Affairs & Patient Safety) and report directly to Jethro Ekuta, Chief Regulatory & Safety Officer, who is based in US.

The position may be based in US or DK, with travel to Ascendis Pharma locations and other business-critical meetings as required.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Lead assigned GRAPS projects and programs from initiation through closeout, establishing clear scope, objectives, governance, integrated plans, milestones, accountabilities, dependencies, budgets, risk controls, and measurable outcomes

• Partner with GRAPS leaders to translate strategic priorities into roadmaps and sequenced execution plans, while maintaining a consolidated view of the GRAPS project portfolio, including capacity constraints, interdependencies, risks, and decisions requiring leadership attention

• Establish and facilitate fit-for-purpose governance, steering forums, workshops, stage reviews, and decision-making processes, and prepare concise executive dashboards, status reports, decision materials, and recommendations

• Coordinate stakeholders across Regulatory Affairs, Patient Safety, Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Quality, IT, Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, and external partners, creating clarity around roles, responsibilities, interfaces, and handoffs

• Drive operational excellence and sustainable change by identifying opportunities to standardize, simplify, and scale processes, tools, and ways of working while supporting applicable GxP, regulatory, pharmacovigilance, documentation, training, inspection-readiness, and records-management requirements

You will also provide project-methodology guidance and coaching to workstream leads and more junior project-management colleagues and may coordinate contractors or matrixed team members.

Qualifications and skills

You hold a relevant academic degree, preferably a bachelor's or master's degree in life sciences, business, project management, engineering, or a related discipline, and have at least 8 years of relevant experience from the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or another highly regulated industry.

Furthermore, you have:

• Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, programs, or major workstreams involving senior stakeholders, multiple functions, geographies, vendors, or systems

• Strong command of project and program management disciplines, including scope, schedule, governance, resources, budgets, dependencies, risks, issues, change control, and benefits realization

• Working knowledge of drug development and commercialization, preferably combined with experience in Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Patient Safety, Quality, Regulatory Operations, or a closely related function

• Experience creating executive-ready dashboards, status reports, decision materials, and presentations using Microsoft 365 and relevant project-management or reporting tools

• A project-management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent is preferred. Agile or change-management training would be considered an advantage

Key competencies

You have an enterprise mindset and a strong patient focus, combined with sound judgment regarding business, quality, compliance, and reputational risk.

You are highly structured, analytical, and detail-oriented while maintaining a clear focus on strategic objectives and outcomes. You can simplify complexity, frame options, recommend a path forward, and communicate decisions clearly to executive, technical, and operational audiences.

You are an experienced stakeholder manager who can build alignment, create accountability, and influence without formal authority. You are comfortable working with ambiguity, managing competing priorities, and adapting plans when business needs change.

As a person, you are collaborative, inclusive, culturally aware, and effective in a global matrix organization. You demonstrate high integrity, discretion, ownership, and a strong commitment to transparent communication and follow-through.

Travel: 15-25 days a year.

Office: Ascendis Pharma, Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup

Apply now

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform. Applications sent by email or through other channels will not be evaluated.

You can learn more about Ascendis Pharma by visiting our website.

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

A note to recruiters

We do not allow external search party solicitation. Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team, specifically from a Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director, is not allowed. If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in hydrothermal liquefaction of biomass and wastes
jobs.description:
Postdoc position in hydrothermal liquefaction of biomass and wastes
The Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, Aarhus University, invites applications for a two separate fixed term positions offering applicants an exciting opportunity to join a new research project on Hydrothermal Liquefaction. One position is for 2 years and one for 1.5 years. 

Expected start date and duration of employment
These are positions from 1 January 2027. There are two positions available, one position is for 2 years and one for 1.5 years.

Job description
The main responsibilities of the candidate will lie in:

• planning and execution of pilot scale HTL campaigns 
• carrying out wet-oxidation experiments in pilot scale
• supporting full scale HTL experimental campaigns with sampling, data analysis, process evaluation and product analysis
• developing new solutions and technologies for HTL product separation at pilot scale 
• Troubleshooting, modification, maintenance and carrying out improvements and upgrades on existing HTL-WO pilot plant
• chemical analysis of HTL products, data processing and analysis from experimental campaigns to produce scientific publications and reports 
• active participation in the project with all it’s partners, attend meetings, compile collaborative reports etc. 
• active participation in the supervision and training of MSc, BSc and PhD students
The work will expand on the on-going research using a state of the art, continuous, hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) reactors at the Foulum Campus of Aarhus University. The HTL plant is integrated with Wet Oxidation (WO) plant is currently one of the largest worldwide in academic settings and allows testing of unique and novel ideas at a relevant scale for industry. The work will be carried out as part of a team working in hydrothermal processing and related technologies. 

Your profile
Prior experience in operation, design and maintenance of chemical engineering processes at lab or pilot scale is desired. The candidate is required to have a PhD in chemical engineering, process engineering or similar (or about to complete the degree). A strong academic background in applied research and publication record are expected. The candidates must demonstrate ability to conduct basic and applied interdisciplinary research, and experience with technology transfer from university to industry is beneficial. 

Experience in analysis of biomass, biofuels and bioproducts using equipment such as elemental analysis, NMR, GC-MS and similar are essential skills for the candidate. 

The ideal candidate has all or several of the following qualifications and specific competences:

• A PhD degree in Chemical Engineering or similar (or about to)
• Prior experience in hydrothermal liquefaction, wet oxidation, pyrolysis, hydrotreating or similar 
• Prior experience in operating continuous reactors for biomass processing 
• A solid background in thermochemical processing of biomass, biorefining, biofuels or related areas.
• The ability to work independently and to generate new ideas and creative approaches.
• The ability to write high impact, peer reviewed academic publications. 
• Is passionate about science and engineering and working in a team dedicated to the green transition.
Who we are
At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering we focus on living systems, the biology of organisms, efficient production, and transformation of chemicals, materials and energy. We translate knowledge within biotechnology, food technology, environmental technology, chemical engineering, industrial biotechnology, medical biotechnology and electrochemical engineering etc. more into new technologies and value-creating solutions that can also be used in the business community.

Many of our research and development activities are based on companies' specific innovation needs or specialist application areas. Close collaboration with the public sector and private businesses ensures that the knowledge and technology generated in the department's research environments has a clear anchoring in reality and benefits the surrounding society. We also provide research-based public sector consultancy and advice on technology in agriculture and food.

At the department, we educate BEng, BSc and MSc graduates in engineering for Danish society.

Read more about the department and sections here:
https://bce.au.dk/en/research/key-areas-in-research-and-development

What we offer 
The department/centre offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment 
The position includes two permanent workplace addresses in Foulum and Aarhus respectively. The attendance at each workplace address is by agreement with your immediate supervisor. At the time of employment, the distribution between the workplace addresses is expected equally distributed with place of employment in Aarhus and Foulum. In Aarhus the place of work is Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, Hangøvej 2, 8200 Aarhus. In Foulum the place of work is Burrehøjvej 43, 8830 Foulum . The area of employment is Aarhus University with affiliated institutions.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associate Professor, Patrick Biller, pbiller@bce.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 25 October 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

jobs.occupation: The Danish School of Education (DPU) at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University, invites applications for a position as an associate professor in educational and developmental psychology, commencing on 1 March 2027.
jobs.description:
Associate Professor in Educational and Developmental Psychology  

This is a full-time position commencing on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The position is based at DPU, at either the Aarhus campus or the Emdrup campus in Copenhagen. The selected applicant will be expected to participate in day-to-day activities at the school, including teaching and supervision. Some travel should be expected between the school’s campuses in Aarhus and Copenhagen. 

The position  

The position involves research and university teaching in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will help further develop the existing research and teaching environment within the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, with a particular focus on developmental psychology in early childhood. 

The position involves teaching at Master’s level and conducting research in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will become part of a well-established academic environment within the Department 

The selected applicant should be able to document experience conducting empirical research, both independently and in collaboration with others, including studies within childhood developmental psychology, using qualitative, quantitative and/or mixed methods. 

Preference will be given to applicants who can document an interest in one or more of the following research areas: Transitions between institutions and families; family life, children’s psychological, emotional and relational development in and across different settings. 

Preference will be given to applicants able to teach and supervise in psychological and educational assessments and psychometrics. 

Research  

The selected applicant will be expected to: 

• develop new research projects relevant to the field of educational and developmental psychology 
• contribute to collaborative research initiatives at DPU, both nationally and internationally 
• pursue external research funding 
• contribute to theoretical, methodological and empirical developments in the fields of early childhood and/or childhood studies and/or family studies. 
• Applicants must outline their vision and plans for contributing to the suggested research fields. 
Teaching  

The selected applicant will teach and supervise students at all levels across relevant degree programmes at DPU, particularly the Master’s degree programme in educational psychology, including the specialisation in educational psychological counselling (PPR) and related electives, as well as in the field of early childhood. Teaching may also be expected on the professional Master’s degree programme in well-being. 

Talent development  

Associate professors at DPU/AU are expected to continuously develop their competences in supervising students at the Master’s and PhD levels, including the development and teaching of PhD courses focusing on theory, methodology and/or specific methods in collaboration with colleagues. Applicants are invited to describe their experiences of and plans or ideas for talent development. 

Knowledge exchange  

The selected applicant will be expected to engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy of the Faculty of Arts, for instance through collaboration on research with external partners, public dissemination activities, consultancy work or collaboration with relevant stakeholders. Applicants should document any prior experience of knowledge exchange activities and outline their plans for maximising the impact of their research within educational and developmental psychology and its implications for practice. 

Qualifications  

Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent qualifications in a relevant field and be able to document: 

• a research profile within developmental psychology in the fields of daycare/reception class and/or family life, as well as children’s psychological and relational development in early childhood 
• an international publication profile, including experience of participation in international networks 
• experience applying for and obtaining external research funding 
• knowledge of and interest in psychodynamic–relational theories of personality, identity and selfhood from a developmental perspective, whether from a supportive and/or a critical position. 
• experience conducting empirical research, preferably using a range of methodologies relevant to the field of developmental psychology 
• knowledge of psychological tests and assessment tools relevant to early childhood and developmental psychology. 
Further information  
For further information about the position, please contact the head of the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, Charlotte Mathiassen, email: cham@edu.au.dk, tel.: +45 6186 3645. 

The application must be submitted in English. 

About the Danish School of Education  

The Danish School of Education (DPU) is one of the three schools at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University. 

Across its two locations at Campus Emdrup in Copenhagen and Nobel Park in Aarhus, DPU is home to approximately 200 academic and administrative staff, as well as approximately 80 PhD students. 

Our degree programmes  

The Danish School of Education currently offers a Bachelor’s degree programme in educational studies and ten Master’s degree programmes in a range of educational and pedagogical disciplines, as well as six professional Master’s degree programmes that can also be studied as single-subject courses. 

Approximately 2,000 students are enrolled in the school’s Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programmes, with approximately 250 students enrolled in professional Master’s degree programmes. 

Many of these programmes are offered at DPU’s locations in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, with students fairly evenly divided between the two campuses. 

Our research  

The Danish School of Education is Denmark's largest university environment for basic and applied research in pedagogy and education. 

The school is home to strong research environments within educational studies, educational theory and curriculum studies, general education, educational psychology, educational anthropology, educational sociology and educational philosophy, 

In addition, we conduct interdisciplinary research focused on specific educational fields of inquiry, particularly schools and early childhood education and care. 

DPU promotes public awareness of research in education and pedagogy through extensive dissemination activities with the aim of providing society with a rich and robust knowledge base. 

International applicants  

International applicants are encouraged to read about family and work-life balance as well as the attractive working conditions and other benefits of working at Aarhus University and in Denmark, including healthcare, paid holidays and, if relevant, maternity/paternity leave, childcare and schooling. Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including a relocation service and career counselling for expat partners. For information about taxation, see the taxation aspects of international researchers’ employment by AU. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here: http://international.au.dk/research/ 

An appointee who does not speak Danish will be required to acquire proficiency in Danish to handle tasks, including administrative and managerial responsibilities, and to participate fully in the activities of the Danish School of Education within approximately two years of commencing the appointment. These activities include, but are not limited to, teaching and examining students, reading work-related texts and participating in meetings and collegial gatherings in Danish. 

Formalities
• Faculty of Arts refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities (the Appointment Order).
• Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.
• Further information on the application and supplementary materials may be found in Application Guidelines.
• The application must outline the applicant's motivation for applying for the position, attaching a curriculum vitae, a teaching portfolio, a complete list of published works, a research plan, copies of degree certificates and no more than five examples of academic production (mandatory).
Please upload this material electronically along with your application.

If nothing else is noted, applications must be submitted in English. Application deadline is at 11.59 pm Danish time (same as Central European Time) on the deadline day.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Shortlists may be prepared with the candidates that have been selected for a detailed academic assessment. A committee set up by the head of school is responsible for selecting the most qualified candidates. See this link for further information about shortlisting at the Faculty of Arts: shortlisting

Terms of employment
• Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations.
• Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as (xxx) at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).
The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

About ArtsThe Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. Within this broad academic scope, the faculty comprises approximately 700 researchers, 200 PhD students, 9,000 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students, and 1,500 further and continuing education students. We believe that the best ideas arise when different perspectives meet – and that research, teaching and innovation are best developed in dialogue with the surrounding society.

You can find more information here: Faculty of Arts | Aarhus University

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Impact You'll Make

At Danfoss, great decisions start with great data. As our new Student Worker in Production Engineering, you will play a hands-on role in building the documentation and data foundation that drives smarter, faster decisions across our production environment. Your working hours will be split equally between our sites in Christiansfeld and Marsvej (Kolding), so you will be working on the production floor at both locations.

You will help uncover where processes can be stabilized, improved, and made more transparent. Whether it is through a well-structured analysis or a small improvement initiative you take ownership of, the work you do here creates real operational value, and you will see the results directly.

This is a role for someone who is curious, self-driven, and ready to work where engineering meets data. You will move between your desk and the production floor across both sites, collaborating with operators, engineers, and supervisors who are genuinely invested in making things better.

What You’ll Be Doing

• 
Strengthen production documentation by creating, maintaining, and improving process records that give the whole team a clearer picture of how work gets done.

• 
Turn data into decisions by analysing production output and preparing insights that support continuous improvement across the organization.

• 
Dig into production challenges alongside engineers and operators to identify root causes and flag where process stabilization is needed.

• 
Drive small improvement initiatives end-to-end, from identifying the opportunity based on data to proposing and testing your own solutions.

• 
Support the production engineering team with a varied mix of tasks, giving you broad exposure to engineering operations in a real industrial environment.

What We're Looking For

• 
Strong Excel skills and a solid foundation for working with and interpreting data.

• 
A curious, problem-solving mindset. You ask questions, explore issues, and aren't afraid to form your own view.

• 
The ability to work autonomously and take ownership, managing your time independently while knowing when to collaborate.

• 
Good written and spoken English. Danish is a plus in our day-to-day team environment.

Do you have solid experience from an industrial or manufacturing environment, and do you thrive in a setting where not everything has been fully built or established yet? Then we would very much like to hear from you.

👉 Read more about the role in the below job description.

Job description

The position:

As Mechanical engineer, you will play a hands-on role in establishing, stabilizing, and improving the mechanical performance of our first-of-a-kind tile production facility in Ikast. This role will work closely together with Operations, Maintenance, Quality, and Process Engineering to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient plant performance. You will help translate innovative process science into robust day-to-day manufacturing at the first of a kind facility, while driving structured problem-solving, equipment reliability, ppm, plant expansion support, and continuous improvement across the facility.

You will support the scaling of this process to our first commercial facility from engineering design and equipment selection through commissioning, start-up, and operations working together with our project department and our EPC firms.

Responsibilities also include:

• 
Mechanical Operations & Equipment Reliability

• 
Provide day-to-day supervisory and execution support for electrical and mechanical systems and production equipment across the tile manufacturing process.

• 
Lead troubleshooting and root cause analysis for mechanical failures, downtime events, and recurring equipment issues.

• 
Help establish preventive and predictive maintenance routines for critical equipment, utilities, and production assets.

• 
Support commissioning, start-up, and scale-up activities in a FOAK environment, helping to translate development work into reliable plant operation.

• 
Production Support & Continuous Improvement

• 
Partner with Operations and Quality teams to improve equipment performance, uptime, process stability, and product consistency.

• 
Contribute to waste reduction, line efficiency, and standardization efforts as production scales.

• 
  Technical leadership

• 
Support the development of SOPs, technical work instructions, equipment care standards, and troubleshooting guides.

• 
Coordinate with vendors, contractors, and internal teams on equipment modifications, installation work, and performance improvements.

• 
Project engineering and commercial facility scale-up

• 
With the Director of projects and an EPC firm, act as Biomason’s lead mechanical engineer supporting the development of FEL3 and detailed engineering design packages including participation in and review of Block Flow Diagrams (BFDs), Heat and Material Balances (HMBs), Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), General Arrangements (GAs), Basis of Design (BoD) documents, equipment specification and selection, and HAZOP (Hazard an Operations study).

• 
Support the commissioning and startup of the commercial facility through:

• 
Participation in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) at vendor sites as needed and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) at the facility.

• 
Provide on-site technical leadership during the "boots-on-the-ground" commissioning phase, troubleshooting mechanical, thermal, or other deviations in real-time.

• 
Bridge the gap between EPC firms and internal operations to ensure a seamless handover.

jobs.description:
At Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to saving and improving lives by unlocking the power of the immune system. Our commercial portfolio includes market-leading vaccines against smallpox/mpox, rabies, tick-borne encephalitis, typhoid fever, and cholera. We excel in R&D innovation, manufacturing, and commercialization, working every day to protect people’s health and quality of life and protect our tomorrow.

We are looking for an experienced leader for the Head of Center of Excellence (project management) role in our Strategy Execution department who combines strategic thinking, strong change management capabilities, and a genuine passion for building organizational capability. In this role, you will not only define how projects are governed and delivered but also drive the adoption of new ways of working across a global organization.

**About The Role

**This is a broad and hands-on role spanning project leadership and organizational capability building within project excellence. A key aspect of the role is driving organizational change by ensuring that project management frameworks, tools, and processes are successfully adopted, understood, and embedded across the business. In this dual role, you will balance being Head of Center of Excellence while managing high-impact cross-functional projects yourself. Just as importantly, you will turn standards into practice by designing and delivering training, facilitating sessions, coaching colleagues, and creating engagement across the organization.

You will work across R&D, manufacturing, supply chain, commercial, and corporate functions. The portfolio may include merger and acquisition activities, development projects, vaccine launches, technology implementations, and other enterprise-wide transformation initiatives. Success requires someone who enjoys moving between strategic planning, practical implementation, and visible facilitation in front of an audience.

The position is based in Hellerup, Denmark. You will join a team of +20 Project Managers, Program Leads, and Student Assistants and report to the VP of Strategy Execution Office.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Own and continuously strengthen project management standards, governance, tools, templates, and ways of working across the organization

• Lead complex, cross-functional strategic projects, including initiatives connected to M&A, product development, vaccine launches, and enterprise transformation

• Drive adoption of project management methodologies and support organizational change through stakeholder engagement, communication, training, and coaching

• Develop project management capability through structured training, facilitation, coaching, and hands-on knowledge sharing across different functions and seniority levels

• Serve as a visible ambassador for project excellence, translating methodology into clear, practical, and engaging learning experiences

• Partner with senior stakeholders to create alignment, transparency, sound decision-making, and clear ownership throughout the project lifecycle

• Drive disciplined planning, risk management, resource coordination, and execution, supported by strong use of project and portfolio management tools

**What You Bring

**You bring extensive experience leading complex projects within pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, vaccines, or another highly regulated healthcare environment. You also bring change management expertise combined with hands-on delivery experience. Besides this, we are looking for someone with the following background;

• A genuine interest in the full scope of project management excellence, from strategic framework design and governance to practical implementation and organizational training

• Strong presentation and facilitation skills, with the confidence and energy to stand in front of an audience, engage participants, and make complex methods practical and relevant

• Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, create buy-in, and lead through complex global and cross-functional environments

• Strong knowledge of PMI-based project management practices. PMI/PMP certification is an advantage - other relevant certifications are also valued

• Experience with merger and acquisition projects

• A relevant master’s degree within life sciences, engineering, supply chain, business, or a related field

• Advanced expertise in Smartsheet combined with experience with Microsoft Project is an advantage

**Why join us?

**This role gives you the opportunity to influence both how strategic projects are delivered and how project management capability is built across Bavarian Nordic. You will combine high-impact project leadership with the chance to shape standards, develop colleagues, and create a lasting project excellence culture in a purpose-driven global vaccine organization.

If you are motivated by strategy and execution, enjoy building practical solutions, and feel energized by training and engaging others, we would love to hear from you.

**Caught your interest?

**Apply now and join Bavarian Nordic in our mission to improve health outcomes and foster sustainable growth.

We do not offer any relocation packages for this role. Please note that employment is contingent on residing and working in Denmark.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

Would you like to manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets – and use your quantitative skills to make better commercial decisions?

Join our Physical Asset Management team and take responsibility for your own areas of the portfolio. You will work hands-on with market analysis, quantitative models, pricing and PnL while building the market knowledge needed to spot where we can do things better.

The team

You will join Physical Asset Management at Norlys Energy Trading in Aalborg. We manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets, combining portfolio management with market analysis and quantitative methods. The work involves close interaction with colleagues across trading, origination and asset management.

The role

As a Quant Researcher, you will operate and develop parts of our renewable portfolio across Europe. Over time, you will become the go-to person for your areas of responsibility: understanding what moves the market, how it affects the portfolio and where there is room to improve performance.

The role has a strong quantitative element. You will build models to understand portfolio effects, develop PnL dashboards and work on pricing methodologies and trading automation. You will also investigate new markets and products and help turn promising ideas into new business.

Key responsibilities

The role combines running the portfolio today with improving how we work tomorrow. You will work independently on some areas and together with colleagues and stakeholders in others.

• Maintain and operate our renewable portfolios across the EU.

• Run your own areas of responsibility with a focus on profitable performance.

• Follow your markets closely and build specialist knowledge within your areas.

• Build and maintain quantitative models to analyse and optimise portfolio effects.

• Develop pricing methodologies and identify ways to improve portfolio performance.

• Build and maintain dashboards that show PnL for your portfolios.

• Help automate trading tools and processes.

• Investigate new markets and products that could create new business opportunities. Work closely with key stakeholders and take part in relevant conferences and excursions.

The people who thrive in this kind of role are the ones who stay curious when the answer isn’t obvious. You’ll have room to dig into problems, form your own view and act on what you learn. And when the market changes, you need to be comfortable changing your mind with it.

Peter Lumbye Thomsen

Head of Intraday Analytics

You are comfortable working with numbers, code and complex market information, but analysis is not an end in itself for you. You want to use it to make decisions, improve the way we work and move things forward when the market changes.

• An advanced degree in a quantitative field such as physics, economics, data science or mathematics.

• Strong programming skills in Python, R or a similar language.

• Experience with data analysis and statistical modelling.

• Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

• A can-do attitude and a sense of urgency when something needs to move.

• An understanding of why agility and speed-to-market matter in a changing market.

• The ability to work well with different stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

• Experience within power trading or finance is an advantage, but not a requirement.

What we offer

• The role gives you room to build specialist knowledge while working hands-on with renewable portfolios across European power markets.

• Your own areas of responsibility within renewable portfolio management.

• The chance to build specialist knowledge of European power markets.

• A role that combines quantitative work with commercial decision-making.

• Exposure to new markets, products and business opportunities.

• Close collaboration with colleagues and stakeholders across the business.

• Participation in relevant conferences and excursions.
